simple.meaning: שָׁגָה (shâgâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to stray (causatively, mislead ), usually (figuratively) to mistake , especially (morally) to transgress ; by extension (through the idea of intoxication) to reel , (figuratively) be enraptured.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 21 times across Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Samuel, Job, and 4 more, beginning at Leviticus 4:13. Its contexts include family line, commandment, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁגָה (H7686).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שָׁגָה (shâgâh) / H7686 is traced through Leviticus 4:13, Numbers 15:22, Deuteronomy 27:18, 1 Samuel 26:21 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: “ ‘If the whole congregation of Israel sins, and the thing is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they have done any of the things which Yahweh has commanded not to be done, and are guilty;
“ ‘When you err, and don’t observe all these commandments which Yahweh has spoken to Moses—
‘Cursed is he who leads the blind astray on the road.’
Then Saul said, “I have sinned. Return, my son David; for I will no more do you harm, because my life was precious in your eyes today. Behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.”
“Teach me, and I will hold my peace.
With him is strength and wisdom.
If it is true that I have erred,
With my whole heart, I have sought you.
You have rebuked the proud who are cursed,
You reject all those who stray from your statutes,
A loving doe and a graceful deer—
For why should you, my son, be captivated with an adulteress?
He will die for lack of instruction.
If you stop listening to instruction, my son,
Wine is a mocker and beer is a brawler.
Whoever causes the upright to go astray in an evil way,

They also reel with wine, and stagger with strong drink. The priest and the prophet reel with strong drink. They are swallowed up by wine. They stagger with strong drink. They err in vision. They stumble in judgment.

definitions.full: H7686. shagah [ שָׁגָה ] verb go astray, err (Aramaic שְׁגָא , id. ); — Qal Perfect 1singular שָׁגִיתִי Job 6:24 ; 19:4 , etc.; Imperfect 3masculine singular יִשְׁגֶּה Prov 5:23 , etc.; Infinitive construct שְׁגוֺת 19:27 ; Participle שֹׁגֶה Ezek 45:20 ; Prov 20:1 , etc.; — 1 err, stray , of flock Ezek 34:6 (figurative). 2 swerve, meander, reel or roll , in drunkenness, ב of drink Isa 28:7 (twice in verse); = be intoxicated , Prov 20:1 ; so with ( בּ ) love 5:19-20 , ׳שׁ בָּרֹאֶה Isa 28:7 . 3 go astay , morally, 1Sam 26:21 ; Prov 5:23 ; Job 6:24 ; 19:4 , + 1Sam 14:24 (reading ׳שׁ שְׁגָגָה ) Th We Dr Now (after ᵐ5 ; otherwise Bu HPS); with מן , of ׳י s commands Psa 119:21 ; 119:118 , מִן of words of knowledge Prov 19:27 . 4 specifically commit sin of ignorance , inadvertence Lev 4:13 ; Num 15:22 (P) Ezek 45:20 (compare שׁגג ). Hiph`il lead astray: 1 literal, Participle מַשְׁגֶּה Deut 27:18 ( בַּדֶּרֶךְ ). 2 ׳מַשׁ mentally = mislead Job 12:16 . 3 morally , Participle Prov 28:10 ( רָ֑ע בְּדֶרֶךְ ); Imperfect 2masculine singular suffix תַּשְׁגֵּנִי , with מן of God's commands Psa 119:10 ; + perhaps Job 12:23 leadeth nations astray ( ᵐ5 SvrVer, i.e. וַיַּשְׁגֵּם for וַיַּנְחֵם ).
